prefs.title: Preferences
set.advanced.hint: These change a default the app is otherwise confident about. Leave them alone unless you have hit the exact problem one describes.
set.advanced.mergeKeyOnly.hint: Off (recommended): a merge carries a translation only where the key matches AND the original text is proven unchanged — by SourceStringHash for a .locres, by the source column for a CSV/PO. Anything whose original changed is left untranslated so you retranslate it instead of shipping text written for the old wording. Turn it on only when that proof is unusable, e.g. an old file whose hashes another tool rebuilt, which makes every row look changed.
merge.pick.old: Select your TRANSLATED file (old version) — .locres, .csv or .po
merge.info.locres.title: Merge — how this file will be matched
merge.info.locres.body:
A translated .locres does not contain the original English, only a fingerprint of it (SourceStringHash). The merge uses that fingerprint: a translation is carried where the key matches AND the fingerprint says the original is unchanged. Rows whose original changed are left untranslated, so you retranslate them instead of shipping a line written for the old wording.

You will see how many rows matched before anything is written, and can switch to matching by key alone there. To make key-only the permanent default, use Tools → Advanced settings.
merge.warn.text.title: Merge — for the most reliable result
merge.warn.text.body:
For the best result this file should hold the SAME source language as the new version in its source column, and the translation in its target column. The merge then carries a translation only where the key AND the original text both match — so a line reworded by the update is left for you instead of shipping the old text.

If this file has no translation column, the merge can still run by matching keys alone. Either way you will see how many rows matched before anything is written.
